decisions.decision: Keep vcn-20260812-2153 / subnet-20260812-2149 as the canonical Oracle networking (though no longer the active deploy target)
decisions.rationale: Verified fully wired (route to IGW, SSH open in default security list) before the hosting pivot happened; zero cost to leave in place unused.

decisions.decision: Fixed the Oracle capacity poller's 'out of capacity' retry interval from 60s to 120s
decisions.rationale: Measured that 60s intervals caused 61.7% of subsequent attempts to get rate-limited (vs 0% after 120s), based on transition-probability analysis of the poller's own log. Confirmed the fix via a clean 38-minute run with zero rate-limited hits afterward.

decisions.decision: Pivoted the production hosting target from Oracle Cloud (eu-zurich-1) to Netcup VPS Lite 2 G12s (4 vCPU/8GB/160GB, hourly billing)
decisions.rationale: Oracle's eu-zurich-1 A1.Flex capacity shortage is structural (single-AD region), confirmed via 200+ automated attempts over 10+ hours with zero successes and no ETA. Rejected AWS explicitly per the user's stated aversion to billing risk. Rejected GCP/Azure free tiers as region-restricted/time-limited/undersized. Rejected a managed-Kafka architecture change as a way to unlock smaller free tiers (no viable free-forever option exists). Hetzner CX33 was the first replacement target but confirmed unavailable at every location. Netcup VPS Lite 2 G12s matches CX33's exact spec at a comparable price, and verified directly that its hourly billing option removes the 12-month-lock-in concern an earlier research pass had raised (hourly billing is the same price with zero commitment) and carries none of AWS-style usage-metered billing risk (fixed-spec-box pricing, traffic overage throttles rather than bills).

decisions.decision: Left the Oracle Zurich poller running as a parallel, non-blocking, zero-cost background bet rather than stopping it once Netcup was chosen
decisions.rationale: Costs nothing to leave running; free-forever compute stays worth having if capacity ever frees up, but nothing is being planned around it or waited on.

decisions.decision: Prod and nonprod will not run always-on on the same box; nonprod will eventually be ephemeral (spun up only for CI/Playwright E2E runs, torn down after)
decisions.rationale: Two Redpanda processes plus two JVMs sharing only 4 shared (not dedicated) vCPUs on the chosen server risks real CPU contention if a nonprod CI run overlaps with real prod traffic. An ephemeral model avoids ever needing a second permanently-running box.

decisions.decision: Generated a fresh, no-passphrase SSH keypair (~/.ssh/id_ed25519_netcup_prod) specifically for the new server, distinct from the Oracle plan's passphrase-protected personal admin key
decisions.rationale: The Docker/firewall setup automation needs non-interactive SSH access; a passphrase would block that. This is a deliberate trust-model choice (the private key file becomes a bearer credential for root access), not an oversight -- worth revisiting if the key's handling changes later.

decisions.decision: Do not trust background-task 'killed'/'failed' notifications for long-running poll loops without direct process verification first
decisions.rationale: The Oracle poller reported 'killed' twice this session while genuinely still running (confirmed via process-tree/log inspection both times). Blindly trusting the first report led to briefly running a duplicate poller instance. This is now a standing operational rule, not just an incident report.

decisions.decision: Renamed docker-compose.prod.yml's DB_URL_PARAMS to DB_JDBC_PARAMS (matching 05-01's actual application.properties variable) rather than renaming application.properties to match 05-02's drafted name
decisions.rationale: application.properties was already merged and is the side application code actually reads; docker-compose.prod.yml is pure config with no downstream dependents yet.
